title: IRAPM Operating State File
description: JSON Schema for the persistent operating state file (§6.7). This is the current-state snapshot needed to resume operation. Append-only logs (CB transitions, annual reviews, cycles, alerts, coordination, token checks) are SEPARATE files with their own schemas — not part of this document. Per §9.4.1, the file is written atomically at end of cycle.

schema_version.description: Schema version of this state file. Loader checks this on read; mismatch triggers controlled migration or refusal to start.

last_cycle_id.description: UUID of the most recent cycle that wrote this file. Pairs with cycle log entries for forensic lookup.

last_cycle_at.description: Wall-clock timestamp when the cycle that wrote this file completed. UTC, ISO 8601 with timezone.

phase.description: Current phase. PHASE_3 is a permanent latch — once set, never changes.

phase3_grace_window_start.description: Timestamp when Phase 3 grace window started (all four Phase 3 tokens observed removed on both boxes). Null when not in grace window. Cleared when grace expires (latch) or abort commits.

phase3_grace_pending_abort.description: Set when a token re-insertion is observed during the grace window but persistence has not yet been confirmed across one full daily-token cycle (§10.6.2 Pattern A). On the next daily-token cycle, the system checks if re-insertion persists — if yes, abort commits and grace window clears; if no (transient glitch), this flag clears and grace continues. Null when not in candidate-abort state.

observed_at.description: Timestamp of the first re-insertion observation that started the candidate abort.

tokens_observed.description: Counts observed on each box at the candidate-abort observation.

income_state.description: Orthogonal to phase. Controls whether scheduled withdrawals execute. Phase 2 ignores this flag (no scheduled withdrawals exist), but state changes are still logged.

income_state_changed_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent income_state transition. Used by stopincome_stuck_alert logic to compute paused-duration.

cb_machine.description: Circuit breaker state, the CB1-active timer, and per-path pending-confirmation counters. CB2 has three independent entry paths (signal, Portfolio-low, FI-low), each with its own pending-confirmation counter; CB1↔CB_INACTIVE has signal-based entry and exit counters. The cb2_entry_conditions set tracks which conditions have triggered during the current CB2 episode — CB2 exits only when ALL conditions in this set have cleared with their respective recovery buffers (§6.3.3, §6.3.4).

state.description: Current CB state. Three values only: CB_INACTIVE → CB1 → CB2. CB1 is signal-based only; resource conditions (Portfolio-low, FI-low) trigger CB2 directly, bypassing CB1. CB1 → CB2 has two trigger paths: signal-based (signal ≤ cb2_threshold_rate for confirmation_window_weeks) OR timer-based (cb1_active_timer has been running for ≥ cb1_to_cb2_timer_days).

cb1_active_timer_started_at.description: Timestamp when current CB1 episode began. Null when state is CB_INACTIVE or CB2 (timer not running). When set, used by the timer-based CB1 → CB2 transition: if (now - cb1_active_timer_started_at).days >= cb1_to_cb2_timer_days, transition to CB2 fires immediately and `signal` is added to cb2_entry_conditions.

cb2_entry_conditions.description: Set of CB2 entry conditions that have been active at any point during the current CB2 episode (§6.3.4). Subset of {signal, portfolio_low, fi_low}. Initialized when CB2 is entered (containing the triggering condition); accumulates additional conditions if they independently trigger during the same CB2 episode; cleared on CB2 exit. CB2 exit requires every condition in this set to clear with its recovery buffer — prevents a transient signal recovery during a resource-triggered CB2 from prematurely routing exit through a path that ignores the still-active resource condition. Empty array when state is CB_INACTIVE or CB1.

pending_confirmations.description: Per-path pending-confirmation counters tracking how many consecutive weekly cycles each entry/exit condition has held. Each counter increments when its condition holds, resets to zero when the condition fails to hold. A counter reaching confirmation_window_weeks (default 2) commits the corresponding transition. Timer-based CB1 → CB2 does NOT use these — it fires immediately when the timer threshold is crossed. The five tracked paths cover CB1 signal entry/exit and CB2 entry on each of the three paths; the corresponding CB2 exit checks use the same paths' clearing conditions and recovery buffers (§6.3.3) but are evaluated freshly each cycle from current values plus the cb2_entry_conditions set.

lookback_signal.description: Most recent Synthetic Growth Lookback signal value. For reporting only — CB transitions key off the per-cycle freshly-computed value, not this stored value. This persistence is for the weekly summary alert and operator inspection.

status.description: AVAILABLE means value field holds the most recent successful computation; UNAVAILABLE means signal failed (stale data or coverage gate) on the most recent cycle.

value_pct.description: Signal value as percent (e.g., -10.5 for -10.5%). Decimal-as-string per §2.8 money discipline (though this is a percentage, not money, same rationale applies for float-precision avoidance).

computed_at.description: Timestamp of the cycle that computed value_pct. Null when no successful computation has ever happened.

schedule_state.description: Per-phase schedule_state per §3.13. Phase 1 instance exists from program start. Phase 3 instance is null until Phase 3 triggers. Each schedule_state contains the starting income, trigger year, CPI rate, and frozen_years list.

buffer_state.description: Recomputed annual values for SGOV buffer and cash buffer. Set during phase transitions and annual reviews. Code reads from here each cycle rather than recomputing.

sgov_target_dollars.description: Current SGOV buffer target in dollars (Decimal-as-string). Updated at phase transitions and annual reviews (Phase 1, Phase 3); frozen in Phase 2.

monthly_refill_rate_dollars.description: Monthly SGOV refill rate = sgov_target / 12. Updated alongside sgov_target.

cash_target_dollars.description: Current cash buffer target = current_monthly_withdrawal + cash_buffer_offset_dollars. In Phase 2, current_monthly_withdrawal is 0, so target = offset only.

recomputed_at.description: Timestamp of most recent recompute (phase transition or annual review).

refill_delay_started_at.description: Timestamp when the post-CB2-exit refill delay timer started. Null when no delay is active. Set when CB2 exits (CB2 → CB1 or CB2 → CB_INACTIVE), regardless of which entry conditions cleared. Cleared when the delay elapses or CB2 re-enters during the window.

last_refill_at.description: Timestamp of most recent buffer refill batch. Enforces monthly cadence (no more than one refill per calendar month).

phase2_opportunistic.description: Phase 2 opportunistic swing state (§6.7, §7.5.2.a). Binary state (steady/deployed) plus two pending-confirmation counters tracking the 2-week confirmation windows for deploy and recover transitions. Only meaningful in Phase 2; the binary state becomes moot at Phase 3 latch and the counters are discarded at that time. Initialized to {state: 'steady', deploy_pending: zero-counter, recover_pending: zero-counter} when Phase 2 begins.

state.description: Current swing allocation state. 'steady' = 90% Growth + 10% GBIL. 'deployed' = ~100% Growth, GBIL at residual floor (§7.5.2.a).

deploy_pending.description: Pending-confirmation counter for the steady -> deployed transition. Increments each weekly cycle the signal holds <= phase2_opportunistic_trigger_rate while in steady. Resets to zero when the signal falls back out of trigger range. When cycles_confirmed reaches confirmation_window_weeks (default 2), the deployment commits. Suspended (not advanced, not reset) during Phase 3 grace window; discarded at Phase 3 latch.

recover_pending.description: Pending-confirmation counter for the deployed -> steady transition. Increments each weekly cycle the signal holds >= phase2_opportunistic_recovery_rate while in deployed. Resets to zero when the signal falls back below recovery threshold. When cycles_confirmed reaches confirmation_window_weeks (default 2), the recovery commits. Suspended (not advanced, not reset) during Phase 3 grace window; discarded at Phase 3 latch.

operational_pause.description: Per §11.3, the auto-resuming pause framework. When paused == true, cycles still run but abort after step 1 without entering decision/action layers. Auto-resumes after pause_auto_resume_hours.

pause_reason.description: Identifier for the pause cause. Enum matches the §11.3.1 catalog. Null when paused == false. Three values are Self-healed-weird (auto-resume after 48h): partial_phase_transition, order_rejection, disk_full. Two values are Hard-broke (no auto-resume; require external action): internal_consistency_violation (§7.3.2 step 4), broker_inconsistency (§11.2.14 hard-broke sub-cases). See D-SPEC-8 for the framework.

pause_started_at.description: Timestamp when current pause began. Auto-resume fires at pause_started_at + pause_auto_resume_hours. Null when paused == false.

consecutive_pause_count.description: How many consecutive pauses have fired for the same pause_reason. Incremented when a new pause has the same reason as the immediately prior pause. Resets to 0 when a successful cycle runs OR when a pause has a different reason. At >= pause_consecutive_escalation_count (default 4), alert severity escalates.

withdrawal_capacity_exhausted.description: Indefinite-halt flag for cascade-exhausted withdrawals (§11.2.7, §11.3.2). When true, future withdrawal cycles are suppressed but all other system functions continue. Auto-clears at the next withdrawal cycle when SGOV+FI+Growth above-residual >= current monthly withdrawal demand (i.e., when cash has returned to the account via the §2.9 'cash appears, system reacts' mechanism). No 48-hour timer-based auto-resume.

coordination.description: Master/slave coordination state (§9.4.2). The role field is per-box local-only and NOT serialized into the rsync'd state file — but the other fields are written by master and read by slave.

master_box_id.description: Identifier of the box that is currently master. Slave reads this to determine whether it should promote when master goes stale.

last_master_write_timestamp.description: Wall-clock timestamp of the master's most recent state-file write. Slave compares this to current time to compute staleness.

master_ipv4_last_octet.description: Last octet of master's IPv4 address. Used in the split-brain tiebreak rule (§9.4.3): lower-octet wins.

pendingCounter.description: Counter tracking consecutive weekly cycles a condition has held. Increments when the condition holds; resets to 0 when the condition fails to hold. cycles_confirmed == 0 means no observation in progress (first_observed_at is null). When cycles_confirmed reaches confirmation_window_weeks (default 2), the corresponding transition commits and the counter is reset.

first_observed_at.description: Timestamp of the first cycle that observed this condition holding. Null when cycles_confirmed is 0.

scheduleStateInstance.description: A schedule_state per §3.13 — represents the inflation-adjusted withdrawal schedule for a phase. The tuple (I_0, trigger_year, cpi, frozen_years) determines what the scheduled monthly withdrawal is for any given calendar year.

i_0_dollars.description: Starting monthly income in dollars (Decimal-as-string). For Phase 1 this is phase1_initial_monthly_dollars in 2027 USD. For Phase 3 this is the computed I_0 from §4.1.1 at trigger (30-year annuity sustainability formula).

trigger_year.description: Calendar year when this schedule_state was initialized. Phase 1: 2027 (program start) for production deployment. Phase 3: year of Phase 3 latch event. Range relaxed from [2020, 2100] to [1900, 2200] to accommodate harness simulator scenarios that drive IRAPM against historical market data (e.g., a Phase 3 trigger in 2016 during the GFC-recovery period); the relaxed range still catches actual data corruption while letting backtests work. Operational timeline expectations are enforced at higher layers (scenario loader, new_initial_state, ruleset validation), not in this schema.

cpi_rate.description: Annual CPI rate compounded into the schedule (Decimal-as-string). For both Phase 1 and Phase 3, this equals the canonical inflation_rate (default 0.035) at the time of schedule_state creation. Persisted into schedule_state so that historical scheduled-amount calculations remain reproducible even if inflation_rate is later changed in ruleset.yaml.

frozen_years.description: List of calendar years for which the annual CPI raise was frozen by the freeze evaluation (§7.6.1). Frozen years never apply their raise; they're permanently excluded from the n_raises_applied count in the schedule formula. PHASE 3 ONLY — Phase 1 has no freeze mechanism, so for a Phase 1 schedule_state this is always an empty list.
